definitions.explanation: Achieving maximum results with minimum waste of time, effort, or resources.

examples.japanese: {効率的|こうりつてき}に{勉強|べんきょう}する。
もっと{効率的|こうりつてき}な{方法|ほうほう}はないだろうか。
examples.english: Isn't there a more efficient way?

examples.japanese: {限|かぎ}られた{時間|じかん}を{効率的|こうりつてき}に{使|つか}うことが{成功|せいこう}の{鍵|かぎ}だ。
examples.english: Using limited time efficiently is the key to success.

notes:
A very common modifier in business, academic, and daily contexts. Formed from {効率|こうりつ} (efficiency) + {的|てき} (suffix making na-adjectives). The base noun {効率|こうりつ} is also frequently used on its own.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {効率的|こうりつてき}な{方法|ほうほう}: an efficient method
- {効率的|こうりつてき}に{働|はたら}く: to work efficiently
- {効率的|こうりつてき}な{運用|うんよう}: efficient operation/management
- {効率的|こうりつてき}な{使|つか}い{方|かた}: efficient way of using

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {能率的|のうりつてき}な: efficient — very similar but slightly more formal and less commonly used
- {効果的|こうかてき}な: effective — focuses on achieving good results, not necessarily with minimal waste
- {合理的|ごうりてき}な: rational / reasonable — focuses on being logical and well-reasoned
- {生産的|せいさんてき}な: productive — focuses on output and results

USAGE:
The adverbial form {効率的|こうりつてき}に (efficiently) is extremely common in workplace and study contexts. The opposite concept is {非効率的|ひこうりつてき}な (inefficient).
